summary: FINAL DRAWING SPEC. Design only: gen.py and arch.html were not touched; a throwaway implementation was rendered and measured in headless Chrome in two themes and five fonts (see layout_plan). Each of the five J2 functions is an agentic graph node: an instance of one Interface-library base class AgentNode (children Identity, Adaptation, Priority, Coordination, Audit), five per department of the ONE global org chart, each with its own chat session. Inside every node every step is one work atom (base class WorkAtom = the plugin atom, child BuilderAtom = J2 atom/1): the runtime opens it with goal, constraints, context, work and a check declared first (or refuses it), the node answers through a closed per-stage reply model, code (never the node) runs the check, and the atom closes with a card and an append-only log row, stays open for another try, or ends abandoned with a reason. J2 role rules become schema facts: write scope = the J2 'writes:' list, a Priority reply has no order field, only Identity's replies have a to_requester field, a finding about an atom Audit owns is rejected. DRAWING: EX = 148 (EXC 92 + GAP 10 + STRIP 46; budget 160, slack 12). Five 164 x 197 cards (J2 map-chip mark, persona + J2 stage letters, chat badge 5, six compartments GOAL, TASK, CONTEXT, WORK ATOM YIELDS, VERIFY, CONSTRAINTS; every text at most 24 characters, measured), a comb and a 46 px 'INSIDE EVERY NODE' strip (open > work > verify, close; dashed exits refuse and abandon), a bus up the gutter from the strip to the Workflow graph store (badge 6) and Chat sessions (badge 5), a slim Atom log box level with the strip, band label '5 NODES PER DEPARTMENT', three arrows that now end on the band, and short text edits in 8 existing boxes plus the band label, the aria-label and three arrow labels. The 15 chips, the J2 loop strip, the connector layer, providers, the key and every existing connection are byte-identical to v3 apart from the group shift (checked element by element). FIXED FROM THE THREE REVIEWS: all P1s (the nodes now draw their graph and chat links; five per department is on the figure) and the cheap P2s: Priority rate card, failure policy, two atom schemas, graph-view colour, TASK mapping, 9 px labels, strip look, records hole, band label, Simple view versus cards, per-atom cost, the Chat agent voice. Dropped from the first draft: the four gutter arrowheads, the Audit arc, the initials circle and the atom-orbit view (reasons in not_grounded FN-23). NO QUESTION BLOCKS DEVELOPMENT: the four draft questions are now recorded defaults (FN-2, FN-7, FN-9, FN-4); decision badges on the picture are deferred to the planned decision-badge version, and the decisions carry ids FN-1 to FN-28 so those badges can point at them.

vocabulary.plugin_meaning: GOAL = what done looks like: one observable outcome, required to open an atom. 'sutra-atom open' refuses a missing goal and a banal one (works, done, ok, fix, fixed, good, passes, it runs, no errors). It is the first row of every card ('Goal:'). At unit level the Flow CLOSE stage only asks whether the unit met its GOAL with a runnable check; the plugin has no separate unit-goal definition. In J2 the same word is the first of ATOM_FIELDS (goal, constraints, context, how, expected_output, verification) and the role sentence of each function file.

vocabulary.in_the_node: GOAL on the card = the node's STANDING goal, taken from its J2 role sentence (identity.md:12 and its four siblings). It is not an atom's goal: each atom the node opens restates its own observable goal, and open refuses a banal one. Example: Priority at J2.c opens an atom with the goal 'proposal P-1 is priced GRANT, COUNTER or REFUSE with an envelope'. The department charter (read as the draw.io model 'Goal') is the reference every node reads.

vocabulary.plugin_meaning: Not a field of the atom and not a primitive. The plugin uses 'task' as: (a) the first line of the DEPTH block, TASK: '[what you're about to do]', emitted before any task; (b) the Blueprint line 'Doing: <plain-English task statement>'; (c) an input TYPE (direction | task | feedback | new concept | question) and the 8-phase 'task' workflow type; (d) a dispatch UNIT with GRAIN single or multi (one atom or many); (e) in Flow stage 5 each step of the unit's step_graph is run as one atom, and a step that is itself a problem recurses (halting rule: every recursion ends at an atom or escalates to a human). J2 has its own 'task': the argument of call(fn, reply_format, task, ...), shown to the model as 'YOUR TURN: <task>' after STATE and CHAT, and a ROLE line per function in the UI. The dispatch record's WDP_TASK is a program tracker id and is not this.

vocabulary.in_the_node: TASK on the card = what the node is about to do at its J2 stage(s): J2's ROLE line, in the same order as the stage letters in the tag line (J2.a·d·h). One TASK runs as 1 to n work atoms in turn (Flow stage 5; Priority's bargain is up to four exchanges). Data: AgentNode.task (the standing line) and WorkAtom.task_id (the user's task N and the workflow id the atom served, for cost roll-ups). Naming caution: the figure also says 'task' for the user's job (Chat agent 'for every task it', org chart 'added by task N'); the card label is TASK in capitals and the strip caption says 'a TASK runs as atoms'.

vocabulary.plugin_meaning: CONTEXT = what the call needs to see: context_refs[], plain strings, shown as 'Using:' and never checked for existence. ADR-029 D2 calls an atom Bounded when GOAL, CONSTRAINTS and context are explicit and minimal-sufficient. (The dispatch context manifest with file sha256s is separate and not part of the atom.) In J2 every call gets context(fn) = 'STATE: ... CHAT: ...' and Identity's state is blind to money.
vocabulary.in_the_node: CONTEXT on the card = the typed slice of department state the node's call is given (J2 STATE + CHAT). Each child class declares its own ContextSlice; Identity's slice has no budget, cost, estimate or envelope fields. The slice's field names are stored on the atom as context_refs and shown in the Agent drawer as 'Was given' (J2's label). identity.md still lists 'envelope decisions' in reads; the code strips envelopes, so the code wins (FN-24).

vocabulary.plugin_meaning: The smallest runnable unit: GOAL + CONSTRAINTS + CONTEXT, one dispatch (one LLM call or one skill), then verified; declared surface GOAL / CONSTRAINTS / CONTEXT / WORK with VERIFY as the teeth. One atom open per session at a time ('the sequence IS the workflow'). Every recursion bottoms out at an atom or escalates to a human. ADR-029 D1: one orchestrator per unit and N worker atoms, the worker owns exactly one atom (do the work, verify it, return the contract); D3: a typed return contract; D4: at most 3 attempts.

vocabulary.in_the_node: Every step of a function node is one work atom: an llm atom is one router call; a code-only action (Priority 'within limits: run', Coordination 'queue empty: hand to Audit', the Relay) is a bash atom at cost 0; a question to you is a manual atom. The card line WORK ATOM YIELDS = what one atom of this node produces (J2 'Expected output'). The runtime declares and opens the atom and runs its check (FN-3); the node's reply is its return contract, a closed per-stage pydantic model. J2 already has atoms for builders (atom/1, docs/atom-schema.md, j2.py:307-317); atoms for the five functions are new. One class tree: WorkAtom (plugin core) with child BuilderAtom (J2 atom/1 fields).

vocabulary.plugin_meaning: CONSTRAINTS = what must hold, stored as constraints[{text, check: null}] and shown on the card as 'Limits:'. The check is always null: the plugin records and shows constraints but never checks one mechanically. J2 atom/1 uses the same word ('Constraints: What must never break'); J2's UI uses 'limits' for Priority's money, calls and time envelope.
vocabulary.source: bin/sutra-atom:109,158,262,268; skills/flow/SKILL.md:243-244; J2: j2_ui.html:524-535 (atom card labels), j2.py:307
vocabulary.in_the_node: CONSTRAINTS on the card = the class's never list (J2 'You may not' lists), copied onto each atom as its constraints. Where possible the app makes a constraint mechanical: a field the closed reply model does not have cannot be said; write scope = the J2 'writes:' list; routes = ROUTES. The rest stays prompt- or Audit-judged (see each function's never). The drawn word is CONSTRAINTS, the model's field name; the diagram never says 'limits'.

vocabulary.plugin_meaning: VERIFY = the teeth. The check is declared before the work from a pinned registry (file-exists, grep-count, named-test) with its relevance, and is refused if unknown or vacuous. It runs at close, by the CLI, under a 30 s alarm; a nonzero result keeps the atom open (VERIFY FAILED card, attempt + 1); a named-test script's sha256 is pinned at open and re-hashed at close. A model cannot close an atom by assertion. ADR-032: 'one shared runner, zero context', with a JUDGMENT lane that can be model-graded. ADR-029 D3 allows the verify result PASS, FAIL or WAIVED.
vocabulary.source: bin/sutra-atom:14,47,184-205,283-342; os/canon/decisions/ADR-032-verifier-layer.md (Decision table, rule 5); ADR-029 D3, D7
vocabulary.in_the_node: VERIFY on the card = the check(s) code runs on the node's reply, declared when the atom opens: J2's existing code checks, registered by name (charter-stamp, workable, audience-split; atom-rules, judge-gate; price-kept, within-budget; order-registered; finding-per-item, pass-needs-proof, code-measure-wins; answer-recorded is new). They are run by the Code validator (J2 'Checker (automatic)'), never by the node. Each is a gate (a failing reply keeps the atom open for a retry, then a recovery) or an override (code corrects the reply and records the change). The confidence judge is a model-graded check whose score code computes.

vocabulary.plugin_meaning: The owner's words are goal, task, context, work atom. The plugin's words are GOAL / CONSTRAINTS / CONTEXT / WORK declared on the atom, with VERIFY as the teeth (bin/sutra-atom:13-14). A J2 function call already has the same parts: system prompt (role = goal sentence + may-not list), 'YOUR TURN: task', context(fn), a reply format, and code checks after the reply; J2's atom/1 has goal, how, constraints, context, defined output, verification.
vocabulary.in_the_node: Six compartments per card: GOAL, TASK, CONTEXT, WORK ATOM YIELDS, VERIFY, CONSTRAINTS. The owner's four words come first in the owner's order (WORK ATOM carries 'YIELDS' because the line is the atom's output, J2 'Expected output'); VERIFY and CONSTRAINTS are the two plugin parts that make an atom enforceable. J2 maps one to one: GOAL = role sentence; TASK = YOUR TURN; CONTEXT = STATE + CHAT; WORK ATOM YIELDS = reply format; VERIFY = code checks; CONSTRAINTS = You may not. Code uses the plugin's field names (goal, constraints, context_refs, work, verify) so it can be compared line by line with bin/sutra-atom.

node.definition: An agentic graph node is a node of the department's Workflow graph that has an agent behind it and the Work-Atom loop inside it. AGENT: one chat session (a Claude or Codex session reached through the connector router), its id stored on the node. LOOP: every step of the node is one work atom: the runtime declares it before the work (goal, constraints, context, work kind and a check from a pinned registry), the node's reply must parse into its closed per-stage reply model, code runs the check, and the atom closes (card + append-only log row), stays open for another try, or ends refused or abandoned with a reason. POSITION: the node belongs to ONE department of the ONE global org chart (five function nodes per department; a division of a department has none and opens its department's Identity chat) and hands off only along its class routes (J2 ROUTES). STATE: idle, running, waiting, waiting_on_you or fault, derived from its atoms and shown on the J2 map chip. NEW definition: no plugin or J2 text defines 'agentic graph node'; it is assembled from Flow stage 5 (atoms as leaves of a step_graph), ADR-029 D1-D4 (orchestrator and worker atoms, return contract, 3 attempts), DISPATCH-ENGINE section 5 (session = agent, DRAFT) and the J2 map function node (a chip with calls, seconds, tokens). EXAMPLE, Priority at J2.c: goal 'proposal P-1 is priced GRANT, COUNTER or REFUSE with an envelope'; constraints 'prices, never orders'; context proposal P-1, budget left, spend; work llm via the router (ref J2.c/price); verify price-kept and within-budget.
node.base_class: AgentNode(BaseModel) in the Interface library: a closed model (extra='forbid', strings stripped, like J2's Artifact base class, j2_artifact_models.py:48-50) with the shared fields below. Second base class: WorkAtom(BaseModel) = the plugin atom 0.3 core plus J2's 'owner' and four statuses, with ONE child BuilderAtom(WorkAtom) carrying J2 atom/1's extra fields. Both sit beside the Workflow, Step and Template bases already drawn.
child_classes: Identity(AgentNode): persona Client Lead; stages a, d, h (plus the approval and safety-limit turns). reads (typed slice, no money): brief, requester feedback and decisions, charter, proposals without cost fields, conflicts, audit findings, alarms, recorded rules, chat; BLIND to budget, rate card, workflow costs, estimates and envelopes (j2.py:3053-3090, COST_KEYS). writes: charter, rulings, done verdicts, questions to you (identity.md:5). routes: you, Adaptation, Priority, Coordination, Audit. replies per stage, not one model: intake (to_requester, to_agents, enough), ruling (clause, decision), approval (DENY or ASK; approved), done (workable?), limit (options fixed by code, Identity writes the message). Only Identity's models have a to_requester field; a mixed reply is regenerated once, then the bad part becomes a template (j2.py:3188-3211). Checks: charter-stamp (j2.py:4172), workable (2470), audience-split (3188), answer-recorded (new: the manual atom that waits for you is done when your answer is recorded).

Adaptation(AgentNode): persona Strategist; stage b (also reshape after e, rework after h, lessons). reads: charter, record, results, findings, constraints, capability catalogue, up to 5 lessons and 2 playbooks, budget (rate card only on the classic path). writes: proposals and revisions (plus lessons and playbooks through the Memory chip). routes: Priority, Identity, and Audit or Coordination only to dispute. Owns the planning pre-check (certainty zones and realization stages; first plan of a website run or a full re-plan; a separate confidence-judge call answers yes/no checklists, code computes the score, gate 0.80, up to 3 revision rounds). Reuse an existing workflow (the plugin's FOLLOW) else the smallest new one (CONSTRUCT). Its reply (PROPOSE) has no envelope, grant, order or verdict field. Checks: atom-rules (j2.py:5962-5996, 6123-6138), judge-gate (j2_realization.py:24).

Priority(AgentNode): persona Prioritiser; stage c and the f run-envelope check. reads: proposals, available resources (budget), current envelopes, reported spend; rate_card is an OPTIONAL field (None by default; on only in the classic path, J2_REALIZATION=0). writes: grants, counters, refusals, envelope changes. routes: Adaptation, Identity, Coordination (HOLD) and the builder by code hand-off. replies per stage: pricing (decision GRANT, COUNTER or REFUSE plus workflows with cost and envelope) and run-check (HOLD or REQUEST_APPROVAL; asked only when a limit is passed, otherwise code posts 'allowed' as a bash atom). No order or schedule field in either. Bargain: max 4 exchanges, 15 minutes, 8 AI calls (j2.py:68-70). Checks: price-kept (j2.py:6534), within-budget (6403-6405, 6669-6670).

Coordination(AgentNode): persona Scheduler; stage f (the charter-change Relay runs in its turn). reads: registered workflows, envelopes, triggers, dependencies, locks, schedule. writes: schedule decisions, holds, handoffs, alarms; holds the write lock. routes: Priority, Adaptation, Identity (Audit by code hand-off when the queue is empty). reply: rule + order + holds[{id, missing}]; no price, envelope, verdict or step field. Check: order-registered (code keeps only registered ids in the order and appends the omitted ones, j2.py:6854-6855).

Audit(AgentNode): persona Quality Reviewer; stage g. reads: charter, registered workflow, run record, the result itself, sources, screenshot, code measurements. writes: findings only. routes: Identity (J2 ROUTES also lists Adaptation, but code sends every finding to Identity, j2.py:8969). reply: one finding per done-when item with verdict PASS, PASS_WITH_WARNING, NEEDS_REVISION, BLOCKED_BY_EVIDENCE or POLICY_CONCERN (TO_BE_CONFIRMED is set by code). Independence is structural in J2 (writes: findings only; no route to a builder; reads the result, not its author's report); the app adds a backstop: a finding whose subject atom's owner is Audit is rejected. Checks: finding-per-item (j2.py:8864), pass-needs-proof (8890-8893), code-measure-wins (9179-9194).

lifecycle.rule: Declared before the work. goal (observable; a banal one is refused), constraints, context_refs, work {llm, bash or manual, plus ref} and a verify check (template + args + relevance, from the pinned registry) are written first. Result: status open, attempt 0, and the OPEN card (J2's atom card: Goal, Constraints, Context, How, Expected output, Verification, with the status line OPEN) in the node's transcript. The runtime declares and opens the atom, not the node (FN-3). One open atom per node session.
lifecycle.enforced_by: AgentNode.open_atom() with the WorkAtom validators (plugin bin/sutra-atom:172-280; J2 check_problems j2.py:613-680 and the atom rules at J2.e, j2.py:6123-6138). The card is rendered by the same function (sutra-atom:15-19,279).

lifecycle.rule: Open is refused and nothing is written when: another atom is open in this node session; the goal is missing or banal; there is no check, or it is not in the registry; the check cannot fail (grep-count min below 1; section-not-empty expecting below 1); the verify target is outside the declared touches and outputs; relevance is explicitly empty; a supersedes target is not abandoned. Plugin: one stderr line 'sutra-atom: REFUSED - reason', exit 1, no card. App: AtomRefused is raised and the reason shows as a one-line refuse card in the node's transcript (FN-16).
lifecycle.enforced_by: The same validators as open: plugin bin/sutra-atom:39,181-248; J2 check_problems (j2.py:613-680).

lifecycle.rule: One step = one atom. An llm atom is one router call, allowed only while the atom is open; the router stamps model and effort on the atom and records usage under the atom id (every router call carries an atom_id; helper calls such as the judge, planner, summariser, run review and template-spec generation are charged to the atom that triggered them; the Chat agent's calls go to a per-task overhead atom). Code-only actions (Priority 'within limits: run', Coordination 'queue empty: hand to Audit', the Relay) run as bash atoms at cost 0 so the floor holds and the graph counts them. A question to you is a manual atom: the node is waiting_on_you until the answer is recorded (check answer-recorded). The reply must parse into the node's closed per-stage reply model; a bad parse is a failed attempt (ADR-029 D3). A node may post a message, record or hand-off only while it has an open atom whose write scope covers the target.
lifecycle.enforced_by: The atom floor made explicit (plugin hooks/atom-floor.sh; DISPATCH-ENGINE section 2: allowed iff the open atom's touches cover the target), with a warn-and-log start for store writes (FN-9); closed reply models and routes are hard from day one; J2 _usable and _check_audiences (j2.py:3188-3211, 5998).

lifecycle.rule: The check declared at open runs when the atom closes, by code, never by the node: pinned registry entry; the plugin's 30 s alarm for mechanical checks (the model-graded confidence judge has its own time budget); write-scope re-check; a named-test script's hash is pinned at open and re-hashed at close (mismatch = exit 97). Each registry check is a GATE or an OVERRIDE. GATE: a failing reply keeps the atom open, attempt + 1, last_result and what changed recorded, VERIFY FAILED card; retried within the check's budget (2 tries for function replies, as J2 does: ask, re-ask once; 3 for builder checks, J2 MAX_CHECK_ATTEMPTS; the plugin's cap is 3). OVERRIDE: code corrects the reply at once and records the change, no model retry (order-registered, pass-needs-proof, code-measure-wins, within-budget, workable). After the last attempt code applies J2's recovery for that check: repair (_code_fix), template (audience split), drop (incomplete workflows), accept with the concern on record (verify result WAIVED, as the charter stamp does after two attempts), or stop and ask you through J2's _identity_limit (budget, cycles, turns or the same failure twice; options fixed by code). Then the status is verify_failed (the plugin's STOP-and-surface). Identity's own failures ask you; they are never handed to Identity.
lifecycle.enforced_by: The Code validator as the shared runner (ADR-032 'one shared runner, zero context'; plugin sutra-atom close:283-342; bin/verify-runner.sh is staging). Attempt cap: ADR-029 D4 and DISPATCH-ENGINE section 6; J2 MAX_CHECK_ATTEMPTS = 3 (j2.py:326, builder checks only); J2's retry-once patterns (j2.py:4145-4152, 3188-3211, 5962-6020, 6385-6399).

lifecycle.rule: Check passed (or recovered by code): status closed, closed_by 'verify', ts_closed; one append-only row in the Atom log (schema atom-ledger-v0.3: id, goal, status, verify {template, exit_code}, attempt, model, effort, touches, relevance, ts); CLOSED card (Goal, Result, Proof, Output, Recorded, Ref). Close itself can be refused: the verify target left the declared envelope, or the hash pin no longer matches. Usage rows are already keyed by the atom id.
lifecycle.enforced_by: close_atom() is the only place status becomes closed, so a node cannot close an atom by assertion (plugin sutra-atom:283-370).

lifecycle.rule: Needs a non-empty reason ('recorded, never silent'); runs no check; status abandoned, closed_by manual-override; Atom log row with the reason; ABANDONED card; frees the one-open-atom lock; the only valid target of supersedes (a new approach = abandon + a new atom). Used when a task is cut, held or replaced.
lifecycle.enforced_by: abandon_atom() (plugin sutra-atom:373-391). Who may call it: the runtime only (FN-17; the plugin lets any session).

lifecycle.rule: OPEN, CLOSED, VERIFY FAILED, ABANDONED (and the one-line refuse) are rendered from state by the transition itself into the node's transcript, in J2's atom-card layout with the plugin status as a status line. They appear in the Detailed view only (Agent drawer atom folds, Needs-you strip); the Simple view shows Identity's plain messages to you and never a card (FN-14).
lifecycle.enforced_by: The transition renders them, so no flag and no caller can skip them (plugin sutra-atom:15-19,95-146); this replaces the plugin's Stop hook (hooks/atom-cards-stop-check.sh). Simple view rule: J2 README.md:134-137 and PLAIN_TO_REQUESTER (j2.py:3130-3137).

lifecycle.rule: Only closed, verify_failed and abandoned atoms append a row to the Atom log (the plugin logs only closed and abandoned; FN-18). Failed tries with attempts left live in the atom's tries[]. A node can never write the log.
lifecycle.enforced_by: A controlled writer in the runtime (DISPATCH-ENGINE section 6 evidence ownership: append-only through the controlled writer; plugin ledger_append, sutra-atom:42,361-366,384-387).

links: Chat session: AgentNode.session_id -> Chat sessions (one per node). Identity's session is the department's chat and the only one you write in; the other four open read-only as the J2 Agent drawer (Summary, Conversations, Thinking). A division of a department opens its department's Identity chat (a pointer, not a second session). Drawn: badge 5 on every card and on the stub into Chat sessions.

Org chart: AgentNode.department_id -> the department node in the ONE global org chart (Department records). A department owns five nodes; moving a department keeps its nodes and session ids; merging keeps the survivor's five nodes and files the other's atoms under them as history; splitting creates five fresh nodes from the classes (FN-6).
Hand-off edges: typed by the class routes (J2 ROUTES). An edge is drawn only from a recorded message or record (J2 map rule: no line without a record), with message counts.

Router: every atom's AI step is one router call tagged with node_id and atom_id. The router stamps model and effort on the atom and writes one usage row per attempt (usd for Claude, tokens for Codex) into the Usage and cost ledger keyed by atom id; helper calls are charged to the atom that triggered them (FN-13); the call stays inside Priority's envelope. graph.graph_view: The Workflow graph view keeps J2's three rows (MAPLABEL.rows): You; Management layer; Team layer and deliverables. Management layer = for each DEPARTMENT of the ONE global org chart, its five function nodes, drawn as J2's chip (a pill) labelled persona then function (Client Lead (Identity), Strategist (Adaptation), Prioritiser (Priority), Scheduler (Coordination), Quality Reviewer (Audit)). A division of a department has no function nodes: it is a lens on its department's graph. A function chip is NEUTRAL with a status outline, because in J2 colour means status only (README.md:351, docs/map-schema.md:154): running = double ring, waiting = thick amber '?', waiting_on_you, fault = thick red '!', idle = plain; the state is derived from its atoms (an open atom with a call in flight = running; an open manual atom = waiting_on_you; an unrecovered verify_failed = fault; no open atom = idle or waiting on a named node). The function colours (violet, magenta, teal, blue, rose) are the figure's own and appear only on the cards, chat avatars and rail headers. The chip carries counts: AI calls, seconds, tokens (J2) plus atoms 'n open, m closed' (new). Atoms are not drawn as dots (J2 draws atoms as counts; the orbit view of the first draft is dropped, FN-15). A click opens J2's node panel with 'Go to the function's tab' and 'See conversation and thinking' (the Agent drawer, which is the node's chat, draw.io step 5); the drawer gets an atom list. Edges are speaks_to (dotted, with message counts) and handoff (solid), drawn only from recorded messages and records and only along class routes. Updates: every atom transition and every recorded hand-off re-derives the node in the store and is pushed live (draw.io step 6). Builders (W-n) are step nodes in the Team layer; the code validator and the confidence judge are not nodes. The Simple view is unchanged: only Identity's plain messages to you.
graph.chat_link: Every node row carries session_id (a map provider -> id, because the router can switch provider; J2 calls are stateless, so the context slice is rebuilt each call and resume is only an optimisation). The Chat sessions store keeps one session per node; the node's atoms run as its turns and its transcript holds the atom cards. Clicking a node in the Workflow graph view opens its chat (draw.io step 5): for Identity that is the department's chat, the only one you can write in (J2: only Identity speaks to the Requester); for Adaptation, Priority, Coordination and Audit it is the J2 Agent drawer, read-only, where each AI-call fold becomes an atom fold: header = atom id + status, rows = J2's atom card (Goal, Constraints, Context, How, Expected output, Verification; the plugin's Done when = Verification, Done by = How, Using = Context, Limits = Constraints, Ref = atom id) with the plugin status line OPEN, CLOSED, VERIFY FAILED or ABANDONED, followed by J2's Was given, Reason, Reply and technical details. A department or division node opens its department's Identity session. The Chat agent never writes to you: it hands the task to the department's Identity and shows Identity's replies (org-level questions go to the root department's Identity, FN-8). Cards render in the Detailed view only. A node that is moved or merged in the org chart keeps its session id. Draw.io steps 5 and 7 (each node, department and division linked to its chat) are satisfied for all five functions.
graph.atom_store: Atoms live in the Workflow graph store under their node, keyed <session_id>/<atom_id> (the plugin's .sutra/atoms/<sid>/<atom-id>/atom.json). Terminal rows (closed, verify_failed, abandoned) append one row to the Atom log box (the plugin's .sutra/atom-ledger.jsonl, schema atom-ledger-v0.3 plus reason; append-only; written only by the runtime's controlled writer, never by a node). Per-try results stay on the atom (tries[]). Usage rows go to the Usage and cost ledger keyed by atom_id (the plugin joins its dispatch-ledger outcome rows to the atom ledger by atom_id).

not_grounded: FN-1 Class tree: AgentNode as a base class with the five function models as children, WorkAtom as a base class with one child BuilderAtom (J2 atom/1). The draw.io page lists eight model names (Identity to Evaluation) with no base or child notation; the hierarchy comes from owner rule 3 and from J2's Artifact base class (j2_artifact_models.py:48-50). 'Workflow, Step, Template' as base classes come from gen.py, not from the draw.io page. [badge target: Interface library box]

FN-2 Every step of a function node is one work atom (llm via the router; a code-only action is a bash atom at cost 0; a question to you is a manual atom); retries stay inside the atom. J2 has atoms only for builders; the plugin has no function atoms. Recorded default for the draft's question 1. Coupled strings (change together): strip caption '1 step = 1 atom', label 'every AI step = one atom', router line 'cost per atom: usd and tokens', ledger line 'one record per atom attempt'. [badge target: strip caption]

FN-3 The runtime, not the node, declares and opens the atom and runs the check. ADR-029 D1 and D2 give dispatch and atom construction to the orchestrator and make the worker own one atom (do, verify, return the contract); DISPATCH-ENGINE section 5 (DRAFT) says spawned agents open their OWN atoms; the plugin CLI lets any session open its own. The departure is deliberate: the node is an LLM that returns JSON, and ADR-032 asks for one shared runner with zero context. [badge target: strip 'open' cell]

FN-4 TASK = what the node is about to do at its stage(s), run as 1 to n atoms. The plugin has no task field (nearest: the DEPTH-block line TASK '[what you're about to do]', the Blueprint 'Doing' line, dispatch UNIT and GRAIN, a Flow stage 5 step); J2's nearest is the task argument of call() and the ROLE line. New fields AgentNode.task and WorkAtom.task_id (the user's task N and workflow id, for cost roll-ups). The card shows the standing line, not the live task. Recorded default for the draft's question 4. [badge target: TASK compartment]
FN-5 The card GOAL is the node's standing role goal (from the J2 role sentence); each atom restates its own observable goal. The plugin knows only per-atom goals. [badge target: GOAL compartment]

FN-6 Cardinality: five function nodes per department of the global org chart; a division of a department has none and opens its department's Identity chat (a lens, not a second session). Merging keeps the survivor's five nodes and files the other's atoms under them as history; splitting creates five fresh nodes. The sources give only 'each node (department, division of a department) linked to its chat' (draw.io step 7) and J2's single department. [badge target: band label]

FN-7 One chat session per function node; only Identity's is writable by you, the other four are read-only (the J2 Agent drawer); session_id is a map provider -> id and the context slice is rebuilt each call (J2 calls are stateless). Recorded default for the draft's question 2. [badge target: Chat sessions box]

FN-9 Role rules as schema facts: closed per-stage reply models (extra=forbid), typed context slices, routes, and write scope = the J2 'writes:' list. risks: Volume: one atom per step means hundreds of atoms and cards per run (J2 runs make 100+ calls). Cards live in each node's own transcript and show in the Detailed view only; the graph shows counts; the append-only Atom log and the store grow with every step, so a retention rule is needed (not designed).

Strictness: closed per-stage reply models are stricter than J2's tolerant JSON parsing (llm.extract_json, _usable); expect more retries until the models are tuned; keep J2's regenerate-once patterns inside the atom's attempts.

Hard write scope can wrongly block a legitimate J2 move (for example Priority re-pricing an Identity ruling with J2_FIXES=1, or Audit's findings reaching Adaptation by ROUTES): store writes start in warn-and-log mode (FN-9).

J2's role .md files stop being the source of truth (owner rule 3): the child classes carry goal, reads, writes, routes and never, and prompts are rendered from them; diff the rendered prompts against the .md files to catch drift, and note that identity.md and the code disagree on envelope decisions (FN-24).

Source inconsistencies resolved here: team.md is a PLACEHOLDER (README.md:177) and differs from ROUTES in places (Coordination to Identity, Audit to Adaptation, Priority to the builder); identity.md still says CEO where J2 means the Requester; audit.md says correctable defects go to Adaptation but code sends every finding to Identity; the Flow skill text says orchestrator mode is off while sutra-defaults.json and ADR-029 say on; the atom CLI header promises a refuse card and a hard floor while the code writes a stderr line and the floor defaults to warn; ADR-018 is PROPOSED and DISPATCH-ENGINE.md is a DRAFT (both cited as background only); bin/verify-runner.sh is staging and not wired into sutra-atom close; the canonical Work-Atom spec the CLI cites (FR ARCHITECTURE v1.3 sections 4.0 and 4.1) is not among the allowed sources, so the atom definition is rebuilt from the CLI, the Flow skill and ADR-029.
